irpt-status._build_note: IRPT cell IB-s-16 (PRD row B16). The StatusEnvelope producer, guarded by _authz.guard() per the issuer amendment (rows W2-S9/W2-S10). enforce.py, resolve.py and keys.py are packaged FLAT because every module sits at /var/task in a Lambda, the SAME convention irpt-ycharts-generate already uses for its own flat copies of the same three files; handler.py is directory (IB-s-1) handler.py, reused (never re-implemented) for the one real network call this function makes: an S3 read of the firm directory artifact, never a vendor; checkpoint.py is intake (IB-s-6) checkpoint.py, packaged because manifests.py imports it for the lease/checkpoint store. manifests.py IS packaged (its class/functions are available to a status_loader once one is wired) even though the deployed lambda_handler does not call it yet -- its default status_loader REFUSES rather than fabricating a READY envelope, per status.py NoSuchOperation. manifests.py and checkpoint.py are also imported directly, in-repo, by the recovery-arms harness and by ops/tests. NO LAYER: jsonschema is not required at runtime (validate_envelope is dependency-free by design, cross-checked against jsonschema only in tests). NO LIVE VENDOR CALL: the only network call reachable from this function is directory.handler.load_directory, which is Opal own evidence bucket, not a vendor. Deployed UNWIRED: no route, no schedule, no event source points at this function from this cell.
